title: Make a strong password

cards.text: The FTC says to make your password long. Aim for at least 12 characters. CISA says longer is stronger.
cards.line: A longer password is harder to guess.

cards.text: A long password can be hard to remember. The FTC says a passphrase can help. It is a series of random words separated by spaces. Avoid common phrases, song lyrics, or movie quotes.
cards.line: Pick words that have nothing to do with each other.

cards.text: CISA says to use a different strong password for each account. If someone guesses one, they could get into every account that uses it.
cards.line: One key should not open every door.

cards.text: CISA says do not tell anyone your passwords. Watch for people who call or email and ask you to reveal them.

checks.prompt: Which password is the better choice?
checks.why: CISA says simple passwords like 12345, and pet names or birthdays, are not safe. The FTC says a passphrase of random words can make a long password easier to remember.

checks.prompt: You use one password for your email and your bank. What does CISA say to do?
options: Use a different one for each
Keep it, because it is already strong
Add a number to the end for the bank
checks.answer: Use a different one for each
checks.why: CISA says to use a different strong password for each account. It says reusing a password, even a strong one, puts your accounts at risk.

checks.prompt: Someone calls and asks for your password. What does CISA say to do?
options: Tell them if they ask twice
Do not tell anyone your passwords
Read it out slowly so they can write it down
checks.answer: Do not tell anyone your passwords
checks.why: CISA says not to tell anyone your passwords. Be careful of calls and emails that try to trick you into sharing them.

takeaway: Make it long, make it different for each account, and keep it to yourself.

situations.text: You pick 12345 as your email password because it is easy to remember.
situations.why: CISA says simple passwords like 12345 are not safe.

situations.text: You make a different long password for each of your accounts.
situations.why: If someone guesses one, they cannot get into every account.

situations.text: A caller says they work for your email company and asks for your password to fix a problem.
situations.why: Do not tell anyone your passwords. Watch for calls and emails that ask.

situations.text: A passphrase is a series of random words, and it can help you remember a long password.
situations.why: The FTC says a passphrase can help. Pick words with nothing to do with each other.
